answer: Latency triangulation: at beacon-picked moments, a dozen probe nodes on different continents ping each agent and log round-trip times. Fifty heads on one rack share one latency vector, so identities whose vectors match within noise count as co-located and share one attestation weight. A relay can add delay but never make a host look closer, so spreading heads costs real servers. Farm heads are a lotus of leaves on one stem, timed by one kernel; honest agents sit apart like cairns along a ridge.
